Jan

The month sets a typical unheated-garage guess. Slide it to what your thermometer says.

At 20°F the fresh-food side is already cold. The thermostat barely asks for cooling, so the freezer side drifts soft. That's the January problem.

The garage fridge

The garage got cold, so the fridge thinks it's done. The freezer side isn't.

On many single-thermostat fridges the thermostat sits in the fresh-food side. A cold garage keeps that side happy, the compressor rarely runs, and the freezer warms.

Many manuals list a minimum room temperature around 50–60°F. Typical; check yours.

If the part fails

If the part we put in fails within 90 days, we come back and make it right at no charge. Sample promise

Fix it or replace it?

If the repair costs more than the machine has left in it, we'll say so first.

Worth fixing. A refrigerator lasts about 13 years (typical), so this one has most of its life left.

Typical lifespans; the rule of thumb is: past half its life and the repair is over half the price of a new one, replace it.
